title: Who you serve, how clients arrive, and getting outreach-ready

say: Who you serve, how clients arrive, and getting outreach-ready.
This is the video for Module 1 of Client Acquisition Basics.
Many skilled women are very good at their work, but get clients only by chance, then nothing for weeks.

say: Every client you have ever had passed through five stages. First, a prospect. That is a specific business or person who could need your service.

panel.heading: Five stages from stranger to client
items: Prospect: a specific business that could need you
Conversation: they have replied, even 'not now'
Qualified: real need, can pay, can decide, soon
Proposal: a clear offer with scope, price, timing
Client: agreed in writing and paid a deposit

say: Second, a conversation. They have replied to you, and a reply of any kind, even 'not now', moves them here.

say: Third, qualified. You have checked they have a real need, can pay, can decide, and want it soon enough to matter.

say: For example, Ngozi runs a small bookkeeping service in Enugu. She wants 2 new monthly clients.

panel.heading: Ngozi's daily message number
items: Target: 2 new clients a month
Half of calls become clients: 4 calls
1 call for every 3 replies: 12 replies
3 replies per 10 messages: 40 messages
40 a month is about 2 every weekday

say: She guesses that half of her calls become clients. So for 2 clients, she needs 4 calls.

say: She guesses 1 in every 3 people who reply will agree to a call. So 4 calls need 12 replies.

These are cautious guesses. Replace them with your own numbers after a month.

say: 'I do social media for anybody' sounds flexible, but you cannot search for anybody. So you write an ideal client profile, with four parts.

panel.heading: Four parts of your ideal client
items: Industry: what kind of business?
Size: how big, and who decides?
Location: where can you serve well?
Trigger: what event makes them need you now?

say: Industry. For example, private nursery and primary schools.

panel.heading: Four parts of your ideal client
items: Industry: what kind of business?
Size: how big, and who decides?
Location: where can you serve well?
Trigger: what event makes them need you now?

say: Size, and who decides. For example, 100 to 400 pupils, where the proprietor decides.

panel.heading: Four parts of your ideal client
items: Industry: what kind of business?
Size: how big, and who decides?
Location: where can you serve well?

say: Location. Where you can serve well, such as Kaduna North and Kaduna South.

panel.heading: Four parts of your ideal client

Trigger: what event makes them need you now?

say: And the trigger, the part most people forget. It is a visible event that creates a need, like admissions season for a school. It tells you who to contact and why now.
If you can find at least 30 real businesses in under 20 minutes on Google Maps, your profile is reachable.

say: For example, Halima manages social media. Her old line said she does social media, graphics and content for businesses at affordable prices. Every competitor says the same.

panel.heading: Halima turns vague into specific

say: Her new line says she helps Kaduna nursery and primary schools get more parent enquiries before each admissions season, with weekly posts and forwardable flyers.
Name the client and the result, in under 30 words.

panel.heading: Halima turns vague into specific

say: When you message a prospect, she will check you in seconds. So first, set up a clear profile. Use the free WhatsApp Business app, with your business name and your offer sentence.

panel.heading: Three things before your first message

cards.d: WhatsApp Business with your business name, your offer sentence, contact details and hours.
2 to 4 real examples. A sample clearly labelled 'sample' is honest and still persuasive.
Work out your costs and time in advance, so you never guess when asked 'how much?'

say: Second, simple honest proof. 2 to 4 real examples are enough.

panel.heading: Three things before your first message

cards.d: WhatsApp Business with your business name, your offer sentence, contact details and hours.

Work out your costs and time in advance, so you never guess when asked 'how much?'

say: Third, decide your price range before you talk. For example, Chioma, a designer, worked out that a one-page menu is usually around 40,000 naira, approximately, from her time and costs.

say: Some strangers are not genuine. Before you start work, tick every box.
Check the business is real, talk to a real person, and agree the scope in writing.
Confirm the deposit in your bank app, because screenshots can be faked. Never pay a registration or vendor fee to get a contract. Genuine clients pay you.
And never share your BVN, card PIN, OTP codes or passwords.

panel.heading: Before you accept a new client
items: Business exists and is findable
You talked to a real person
Scope agreed in writing
Deposit received in your account
No upfront fee asked of you

say: So remember. Client acquisition is a skill you can learn. Work backwards from your target to a daily number, and aim at one clear profile with a trigger.
And do not work free to prove yourself. Use a small, clearly priced starter offer instead.

panel.heading: Key points from Module 1
items: Client acquisition is a learnable skill
Five stages: prospect to paying client
Work backwards to a daily message number
Name industry, size, location and trigger
Avoid free work; use a small paid starter offer
